# Introduction

This script performs analysis, performance evaluation, and visualisation of 
a U-Net deep learning model for mapping African baobab trees using 
multi-seasonal satellite imagery. 

The workflow is structured into several sections, each addressing a specific component of the analysis presented in our Manuscript: Chafika Phiri, Hugh A. Graham, Sarah Venter, Dawn Cory-Toussaint, Dave Hodgson, and Andrew M. Cunliffe (2026): “[Title of our Manuscript]”

## **Performance Evaluation**

We conducted object-level validation by comparing manually delineated tree crown polygons. We selected two areas from each site that were well observed and excluded areas that we did not visit, as we do not know whether there were false positives. Each connected group of predicted tree pixels was isolated as an individual object. A match between predicted and the manually digitised crowns were determined by the overlap between their polygons. 

```{r}

#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| messages: false

library(terra)
library(sf)

# clip an area of interest from kremetart

Mapungubwe <- st_read("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Landscape complexity/game_reserve_evaluation.gpkg")

# area of interest (AOI) for evaluation

#total_area <- Mapungubwe |>
#  st_transform(32735) |>
#  st_area() |>
#  sum()

#total_area

# Remove any empty or invalid geometries

aoi <- st_make_valid(Mapungubwe)

# load raster

kremetart_feb <- rast("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Predicted_Maps/kremetart_baobab_july_8.1m_binary.tif")

crs(kremetart_feb)

# reproject to the ratsre crs

aoi_utm <- st_transform(aoi, crs(kremetart_feb))

# convert sf → terra vector

aoi_vect <- vect(aoi_utm)

# crop raster
kremetart_crop <- crop(kremetart_feb, aoi_vect)

# mask to exact polygon

kremetart_clip <- mask(kremetart_crop, aoi_vect)

# Remove surrounding NA cells

aoi_trimmed <- trim(kremetart_clip)

plot(aoi_trimmed)

# check the values in the raster file

unique(values(aoi_trimmed))

# save raster

writeRaster(aoi_trimmed,
            "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Predicted_Maps/Evaluation_Site_Maps/game_reserve_baobab_map_july_8.1m_binary.tif",
            overwrite = TRUE)

```

Plot a descriptive table for the performance metrics (Precision, Recall, F1)
Generate the table to show the total number of baobabs detected in the evaluated site

```{r}

#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| messages: false

library(terra)

# Load the input data-----------------------------------------------------------

reference <- terra::vect("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/game_reserve_baobab_ellipses.gpkg")

#reference <- terra::vect("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Kremetart_evaluation_class_one_tree_polygons.gpkg")

binary_rast <- terra::rast("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Predicted_Maps/Evaluation_Site_Maps/game_reserve_baobab_map_july_0.9m_binary.tif")
fg          <- terra::ifel(binary_rast == 1, 1, NA)
predicted   <- terra::as.polygons(fg, dissolve = TRUE, values = FALSE)
predicted   <- terra::disagg(predicted)

if (!identical(terra::crs(reference), terra::crs(predicted))) {
  cat("CRS mismatch — reprojecting reference to match predictions\n")
  reference <- terra::project(reference, terra::crs(predicted))
}

predicted$pred_id <- seq_len(nrow(predicted))
reference$ref_id  <- seq_len(nrow(reference))
predicted$area_m2 <- terra::expanse(predicted, unit = "m")
reference$area_m2 <- terra::expanse(reference, unit = "m")

cat(sprintf("Predicted polygons: %d\n", nrow(predicted)))
cat(sprintf("Reference polygons: %d\n", nrow(reference)))

# OBJECT-LEVEL EVALUATION-------------------------------------------------------

# Rule: a reference tree is detected if intersects or overlaps a prediction blob

evaluate_detection <- function(predicted, reference) {
  
  pred_n <- nrow(predicted)
  ref_n  <- nrow(reference)
  
  M <- terra::relate(predicted, reference, "intersects")
  
  pred_hits_ref <- apply(M, 1, any)
  ref_is_hit    <- apply(M, 2, any)
  
  tp <- sum(ref_is_hit)
  fn <- sum(!ref_is_hit)
  fp <- sum(!pred_hits_ref)
  
  precision <- tp / (tp + fp)
  recall    <- tp / (tp + fn)
  f1        <- 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
  
  count_err <- (pred_n - ref_n) / ref_n
  
  list(
    pred_count    = pred_n,
    ref_count     = ref_n,
    tp            = tp,
    fp            = fp,
    fn            = fn,
    precision     = precision,
    recall        = recall,
    f1            = f1,
    count_error   = count_err,
    pred_hits_ref = pred_hits_ref,
    ref_is_hit    = ref_is_hit
  )
}

results <- evaluate_detection(predicted, reference)

# print the results-------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("OBJECT-LEVEL DETECTION EVALUATION\n")
cat("(a tree counts once, regardless of how many\n")
cat(" predictions land on it)\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Reference baobabs:   %d\n", results$ref_count))
cat(sprintf("Predicted polygons:  %d\n", results$pred_count))
cat(sprintf("\n"))
cat(sprintf("TP (trees detected): %d\n", results$tp))
cat(sprintf("FN (trees missed):   %d\n", results$fn))
cat(sprintf("FP (spurious preds): %d\n", results$fp))
cat(sprintf("\n"))
cat(sprintf("Precision: %.3f\n", results$precision))
cat(sprintf("Recall:    %.3f\n", results$recall))
cat(sprintf("F1:        %.3f\n", results$f1))
cat(sprintf("Count err: %+.1f%%\n", 100 * results$count_error))


# Save the polygons for ispection

predicted$status <- ifelse(results$pred_hits_ref, "TP", "FP")
reference$status <- ifelse(results$ref_is_hit,    "TP", "FN")

terra::writeVector(predicted,
                   "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/july_nature_reserve_predictions_polygons_evaluated_site_0.9m.gpkg",
                   overwrite = TRUE)
terra::writeVector(reference,
                   "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/july_nature_serve_reference_polygons_0.9m.gpkg",
                   overwrite = TRUE)

```

## the effect of spatial resolution and dataset on the model performance

In this section, we evaluated how changes in spatial resolution and dataset composition affect the performance of the U-Net model.

```{r}

# Performance metrics by spatial resolution and dataset
# Two sites, three metrics (Precision, Recall, F1-Score), four resolutions and datasets

# Load all CSVs into a single combined data frame 

csv_files <- list.files(
  path = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/CSV_logs/Evaluation_Results/Metrics_Summaries/",
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

combined <- lapply(csv_files, function(f) {
  df <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
  df$source <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  df
}) |> bind_rows()

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(
    season = case_when(
      grepl("feb_july", source) ~ "Combined",
      grepl("^feb",     source) ~ "February",
      grepl("^july",    source) ~ "July"
    ),
    site = case_when(
      grepl("kremetart",  source) ~ "Kremetart",
      grepl("mapungubwe", source) ~ "Mapungubwe"
    ),
    resolution = as.numeric(sub(".*_([0-9.]+)m$", "\\1", source))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(site), !is.na(season), !is.na(resolution))

metric_cols <- c("precision", "recall", "f1")

summary_tbl <- combined |>
  select(
    Site                 = site,
    Season               = season,
    Resolution           = resolution,
    `Reference trees`    = ref_count,
    `Predicted polygons` = pred_count,
    TP                   = tp,
    FP                   = fp,
    FN                   = fn,
    Precision            = precision,
    Recall               = recall,
    F1                   = f1
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(Precision, Recall, F1), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  arrange(Site, Season, Resolution)

print(summary_tbl)

write.csv(
  summary_tbl,
  "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Manuscripts Plots/spatial_grain_summ#ary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

long <- combined |>
  select(site, season, resolution, all_of(metric_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metric_cols),
               names_to = "metric",
               values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric,
                    levels = c("f1", "precision", "recall"),
                    labels = c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall")),
    group_label = paste(site, season, sep = " – ")
  )

main_plot <- ggplot(long, aes(x = resolution, y = score,
                              colour = group_label,
                              group  = group_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3.0) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(0.3, 0.9, 2.7, 8.1),
    labels = c("0.3", "0.9", "2.7", "8.1"),
    minor_breaks = NULL
  ) +
```

## the effect of crown sizes on the model performance

This section assesses model performance across different tree crown size classes (small, medium and large) and spatial resolutions. It examines how variations in crown size and image resolution influence detection accuracy, precision, recall, and F-Score

```{r}

# Performance metrics by crown size and spatial resolution
# Two sites, three metrics (Precision, Recall, F1), four resolutions

# ---- Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# ---- load the files ----------------------------------------------------------

site1_path <- "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/kremetart_july"
site2_path <- "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/mapungubwe_july"

resolution_pattern <- "\\d+\\.\\d+m"
resolution_levels  <- c("0.3 m", "0.9 m", "2.7 m", "8.1 m")
resolution_colors  <- c("0.3 m" = "#264653",
                        "0.9 m" = "#2A9D8F",
                        "2.7 m" = "#E9C46A",
                        "8.1 m" = "#d62728")

# ---- Read CSVs from both site folders ----------------------------------------

read_site <- function(folder) {
  files <- list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  lapply(files, function(f) {
    df <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
    df$source <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
    df
  }) |> bind_rows()
}

combined <- bind_rows(read_site(site1_path), read_site(site2_path))

# ---- Derive site, resolution, and file type from filename --------------------

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(
    site_label = case_when(
      str_detect(source, "kremetart")  ~ "Kremetart",
      str_detect(source, "mapungubwe") ~ "Mapungubwe",
      TRUE                             ~ NA_character_
    ),
    resolution = str_extract(source, resolution_pattern),
    resolution = str_replace(resolution, "m", " m"),
    resolution = factor(resolution, levels = resolution_levels),
    file_type  = if_else(str_detect(source, "reference"),
                         "reference", "predictions")
  )

if (any(is.na(combined$site_label))) stop("Some rows have no site assigned.")
if (any(is.na(combined$resolution))) stop("Some rows have no resolution parsed.")

cat("Status values by file type:\n")
print(table(combined$file_type, combined$status, useNA = "ifany"))

# ---- Equal-count crown size bins from reference polygons ---------------------

ref_unique <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "reference") |>
  group_by(site_label, ref_id) |>
  summarise(area_m2 = median(area_m2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bin_breaks <- quantile(ref_unique$area_m2,
                       probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 4),
                       na.rm = TRUE)

bin_breaks[1]                  <- floor(min(combined$area_m2,  na.rm = TRUE))
bin_breaks[length(bin_breaks)] <- ceiling(max(combined$area_m2, na.rm = TRUE))
bin_breaks <- unique(bin_breaks)

if (length(bin_breaks) < 4) stop("Could not form 3 distinct bins.")

bin_labels <- c(
  paste0("Small\n(",  round(bin_breaks[1], 1), "-", round(bin_breaks[2], 1), " m\u00B2)"),
  paste0("Medium\n(", round(bin_breaks[2], 1), "-", round(bin_breaks[3], 1), " m\u00B2)"),
  paste0("Large\n(",  round(bin_breaks[3], 1), "-", round(bin_breaks[4], 1), " m\u00B2)")
)

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(crown_bin = cut(area_m2,
                         breaks         = bin_breaks,
                         labels         = bin_labels,
                         include.lowest = TRUE))

# ---- Precision, Recall, F1 (TP/FP from predictions, FN from reference) -------

tp_fp <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "predictions") |>
  group_by(site_label, resolution, crown_bin) |>
  summarise(TP = sum(status == "TP", na.rm = TRUE),
            FP = sum(status == "FP", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

fn <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "reference") |>
  group_by(site_label, resolution, crown_bin) |>
  summarise(FN = sum(status == "FN", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

metrics <- full_join(tp_fp, fn, by = c("site_label", "resolution", "crown_bin")) |>
  mutate(across(c(TP, FP, FN), ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L)),
         Precision  = ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), NA_real_),
         Recall     = ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), NA_real_),
         `F1-score` = ifelse((Precision + Recall) > 0,
                             2 * Precision * Recall / (Precision + Recall),
                             NA_real_))

# ---- Long format -------------------------------------------------------------

metrics_long <- metrics |>
  pivot_longer(cols      = c(Precision, Recall, `F1-score`),
               names_to  = "metric",
               values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall")))

# ---- Reference polygon counts per site x bin ---------------------------------

n_labels <- ref_unique |>
  mutate(crown_bin = cut(area_m2,
                         breaks         = bin_breaks,
                         labels         = bin_labels,
                         include.lowest = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(site_label, crown_bin) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::crossing(metric = factor(c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall"),
                                  levels = c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall"))) |>
  mutate(label = paste0("n = ", n))

# ---- N labels: total TP predicted by the model per site × crown size ---------

#n_labels <- tp_fp |>
#  group_by(site_label, crown_bin) |>
#  summarise(n = sum(TP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
#  tidyr::crossing(metric = factor(c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall"),
#                                  levels = c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall"))) |>
#  mutate(label = paste0("n = ", n))

# ---- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------

p <- ggplot(metrics_long,
            aes(x = crown_bin, y = value, fill = resolution)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = n_labels,
            aes(x = crown_bin, y = 1.06, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 3, color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(site_label ~ metric) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = resolution_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.12),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(x = "Crown size class", y = "Detection Score", fill = "Resolution") +
  theme_fancy() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1, "lines"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) 
  
print(p)

# ---- Save --------------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Manuscripts Plots/crown_sizes_combined_summary_plot.png", plot = p,
       width  = 21.0,
       height = 14.85,
       units  = "cm",
       dpi    = 600,
       bg     = "white")

```

### Seasonality influence

This section assesses model performance across imagery from different seasons and spatial resolutions. It examines how seasonal changes in vegetation and variations in image resolution influence key performance metrics.

```{r}

# Performance metrics by imagery composition (season) and spatial resolution

# Site 1 only - since we only had two images acquired at Kremetart, therefore comparisons were only done at kremetart

# ---- Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# ----load the files------------------------------------------------------------

season_paths <- c(
  "Single (wet)"     = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/kremetart_feb",
  "Single (dry)"     = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/kremetart_July",
  "Multi (dry+wet)"  = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/kremetart_combined"
)

resolution_pattern <- "\\d+\\.\\d+m"
resolution_levels  <- c("0.3 m", "0.9 m", "2.7 m", "8.1 m")

# ---- Read CSVs from all season folders ---------------------------------------

read_season <- function(folder, season_label) {
  files <- list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  lapply(files, function(f) {
    df <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
    df$source        <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
    df$season_label  <- season_label
    df
  }) |> bind_rows()
}

combined <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(season_paths), function(i) {
  read_season(season_paths[[i]], names(season_paths)[i])
}))

# ---- Derive resolution and file type from filename ---------------------------

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(
    resolution = str_extract(source, resolution_pattern),
    resolution = str_replace(resolution, "m", " m"),
    resolution = factor(resolution, levels = resolution_levels),
    file_type  = if_else(str_detect(source, "reference"),
                         "reference", "predictions"),
    season_label = factor(season_label, levels = names(season_paths))
  )

if (any(is.na(combined$resolution))) stop("Some rows have no resolution parsed.")

cat("Rows per season and resolution:\n")
print(table(combined$season_label, combined$resolution))
cat("\nStatus values by file type:\n")
print(table(combined$file_type, combined$status, useNA = "ifany"))

# ---- Precision, Recall, F1 (TP/FP from predictions, FN from reference) -------

tp_fp <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "predictions") |>
  group_by(season_label, resolution) |>
  summarise(TP = sum(status == "TP", na.rm = TRUE),
            FP = sum(status == "FP", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

fn <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "reference") |>
  group_by(season_label, resolution) |>
  summarise(FN = sum(status == "FN", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

metrics <- full_join(tp_fp, fn, by = c("season_label", "resolution")) |>
  mutate(across(c(TP, FP, FN), ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L)),
         Precision  = ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), NA_real_),
         Recall     = ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), NA_real_),
         `F1-score` = ifelse((Precision + Recall) > 0,
                             2 * Precision * Recall / (Precision + Recall),
                             NA_real_))

# ---- Colours now map to imagery composition (the key comparison) -------------

season_colours <- c(
  "Single (wet)"    = "lightseagreen",
  "Single (dry)"    = "black",
  "Multi (dry+wet)" = "firebrick"
)

# ---- Reshape to long format so each metric can be plotted as its own facet ---

metrics_long <- metrics |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(Precision, Recall, `F1-score`),
    names_to  = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(resolution_m = as.numeric(str_replace(resolution, " m", "")))

# ---- Plot: lines across spatial grain, one line per imagery composition ------

seasonality <- ggplot(metrics_long,
            aes(x = resolution_m, y = value,
                colour = season_label, group = season_label,
                shape = season_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = season_colours) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(
    "Single (wet)"    = 17,
    "Single (dry)"    = 4,
    "Multi (dry+wet)" = 18
  )) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.9, 2.7, 8.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Spatial grain (m)", y = "Detection score",
       colour = "Imagery composition",
       shape = "Imagery composition") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme_fancy() +
  theme(
    axis.title        = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
    strip.text        = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.direction  = "horizontal",
    legend.box        = "horizontal",
    legend.title.position = "top",
    legend.key.width  = unit(1.0, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.margin     = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x   = unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE))

plot(seasonality)

# ---- Save --------------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Manuscripts Plots/seasonality_resolution_summary_plot.png", plot = seasonality,
       width  = 21.0,
       height = 14.85,
       units  = "cm",
       dpi    = 600,
       bg     = "white")

```

## landscape complexity based on the land use type

This section evaluates model performance across different landscape types (National Park, Irrigated Cropland, and Game Reserve) and spatial resolutions. It examines how variations in land cover and image detail influence key performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

```{r}

# Performance metrics by imagery landscapes National Park, Irrigated Crop Land, Game Reserve and spatial resolution

# ---- Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# ---- load the files ----------------------------------------------------------

season_paths <- c(
  "Agriculture Land"     = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/irrigated_july",
  "Game Reserve"     = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/nature_reserve_july",
  "National Park"  = "C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Tree_Crowns_Polygons/Predicted_Polygons/Predicted_Polygon_Areas/mapungubwe_july"
)

resolution_pattern <- "\\d+\\.\\d+m"
resolution_levels  <- c("0.3 m", "0.9 m", "2.7 m", "8.1 m")

# Assumed landscape-complexity, one entry per land-use type.

#complexity_levels <- c(
#  "Agriculture Land" = "configurationally",
#  "Game Reserve"     = "compositionally",
#  "National Park"    = "less"
#)

# Colour per land-use type (lines), replacing the per-resolution palette.

landuse_colors <- c(
  "Agriculture Land" = "#000000",
  "Game Reserve"     = "#2A9D8F",
  "National Park"    = "#d62728"
)

# ---- Read CSVs from all season folders ---------------------------------------

read_season <- function(folder, season_label) {
  files <- list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  lapply(files, function(f) {
    df <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
    df$source        <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
    df$season_label  <- season_label
    df
  }) |> bind_rows()
}

combined <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(season_paths), function(i) {
  read_season(season_paths[[i]], names(season_paths)[i])
}))

# ---- Derive resolution and file type from filename ---------------------------

combined <- combined |>
  mutate(
    resolution = str_extract(source, resolution_pattern),
    resolution = str_replace(resolution, "m", " m"),
    resolution = factor(resolution, levels = resolution_levels),
    file_type  = if_else(str_detect(source, "reference"),
                         "reference", "predictions"),
    season_label = factor(season_label, levels = names(season_paths))
  )

if (any(is.na(combined$resolution))) stop("Some rows have no resolution parsed.")

cat("Rows per season and resolution:\n")
print(table(combined$season_label, combined$resolution))
cat("\nStatus values by file type:\n")
print(table(combined$file_type, combined$status, useNA = "ifany"))

# ---- Precision, Recall, F1 (TP/FP from predictions, FN from reference) -------

tp_fp <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "predictions") |>
  group_by(season_label, resolution) |>
  summarise(TP = sum(status == "TP", na.rm = TRUE),
            FP = sum(status == "FP", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

fn <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "reference") |>
  group_by(season_label, resolution) |>
  summarise(FN = sum(status == "FN", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

metrics <- full_join(tp_fp, fn, by = c("season_label", "resolution")) |>
  mutate(across(c(TP, FP, FN), ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0L)),
         Precision  = ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), NA_real_),
         Recall     = ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), NA_real_),
         `F1-score` = ifelse((Precision + Recall) > 0,
                             2 * Precision * Recall / (Precision + Recall),
                             NA_real_))

# ---- Sample sizes: reference crowns per land-use type ------------------------
# One reference crown is a row in a reference file, so n is the count of those
# rows per land-use type, taken at a single resolution to avoid counting the
# same crowns four times over.

sample_sizes <- combined |>
  filter(file_type == "reference", resolution == resolution_levels[1]) |>
  count(season_label, name = "n")

# ---- Land-use labels: complexity + sample size -------------------------------

#landuse_labels <- sample_sizes |>
#  mutate(complex = complexity_levels[as.character(season_label)],
#         label = str_glue("{season_label} ({complex} complex, n = {n})")) |>
#  select(season_label, label) |>
#  deframe()

landuse_labels <- setNames(
  str_glue("{sample_sizes$season_label} (n = {sample_sizes$n})"),
  sample_sizes$season_label
)

# ---- Long format -------------------------------------------------------------

metrics_long <- metrics |>
  pivot_longer(cols      = c(Precision, Recall, `F1-score`),
               names_to  = "metric",
               values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("F1-score", "Precision", "Recall")),
         grain_m = as.numeric(str_remove(as.character(resolution), " m")))

# ---- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------

landscape_complexity <- ggplot(metrics_long,
            aes(x = grain_m, y = value,
                colour = season_label, group = season_label,
                shape = season_label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.9, 2.7, 8.1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = landuse_colors) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = landuse_colors, labels = landuse_labels) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(
    "Agriculture Land" = 4,
    "Game Reserve"     = 17,
    "National Park"    = 18
  ), labels = landuse_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Spatial grain (m)", y = "Detection score",
       colour = "Land-use type", shape = "Land-use type") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0),
         shape  = guide_legend(ncol = 1, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme_fancy() +
  theme(
    axis.title        = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
    strip.text        = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position   = "bottom",
    legend.direction  = "horizontal",
    legend.box        = "horizontal",
    legend.title.position = "top",
    legend.key.width  = unit(1.0, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.margin     = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x   = unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE))

print(landscape_complexity)

# ---- Save --------------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave("C:/Workspace/Phiri_et_al_baobab_mapping_with_unet/Manuscripts Plots/landscape_complexity_resolution_summary_plot.png", plot = landscape_complexity,
       width  = 21.0,
       height = 14.85,
       units  = "cm",
       dpi    = 600,
       bg     = "white")
```
